Includes this load’s 100% duty cycle and the station’s 9.0 W idle draw — not a label-wattage guess.

0 – 600 W across the rails above

No start-up rail: this start lasts minutes rather than milliseconds, so it was checked against continuous output rather than against a surge rating.

Two numbers decide this, and readers use them interchangeably: watts are the ceiling on what the inverter holds at any instant, watt-hours are how much energy the battery holds. A machine can have plenty of one and not enough of the other.

The verdict is a calculation, not a lookup; the hours are a division, not the nameplate watt-hours. The working is in the evidence below.

Where those numbers come from

A blank is never left blank. A field we have found no figure for says so, and a field whose sources disagree — two documents, or one document with itself — says that instead of picking one.

The surge ceiling on this page is ours, not the manufacturer’s

We have found no published surge rating for the EU 230 V build. So the start-up check runs against the continuous output instead — an inverter cannot surge below what it sustains, which makes that the safest number we can defend. Real inverters usually manage 1.5–2× their continuous rating, so a start-up call held back by this figure may well be fine in practice; we are not going to say so until the manufacturer does.

Questions people ask about this pairing

Will a BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 run a diesel air heater?
Yes. 34 W of running draw against 600 W of continuous output — 5.7% of it. The verdict is computed from running watts, start-up inrush, and inverter waveform — the working is in the evidence section above.
How long will a BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 run a diesel air heater?
About 5.7 hours on a full charge. That divides a usable-capacity figure derived from BLUETTI's own published depth of discharge and inverter efficiency by this load's duty-weighted draw plus the machine's own 9.0 W idle draw — not the nameplate watt-hours divided by a label wattage, which is where the confident-looking 20–35% overstatements come from.
Where does the surge ceiling for the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 come from?
From us, and the page says so every time it uses it. We have found no published surge rating for the EU 230 V build. So the start-up check runs against the continuous output as a conservative floor — an inverter cannot surge below what it sustains. Real inverters usually manage 1.5–2× their continuous rating, which means a start-up call held back by this figure may well be fine in practice. We will not say so until the manufacturer publishes a number.
